newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremer Vulkan rebirth a possibility - reports.
newsitem.headline: Bremer Vulkan rebirth a possibility - reports.

text.p: Collapsed German shipbuilder Bremer Vulkan could be resurrected if a legal bankruptcy settlement is successfully negotiated with the group's creditors, German newspapers said at the weekend.

The Welt am Sonntag newspaper said that Ulrich Noelle, a member of the Bremen senate with responsibility for finance, is attempting to resurrect the shipbuilder and with this provide new jobs in the area.

The Bremer Vulkan group collapsed spectacularly in May 1996 after posting huge losses and being accused of having misappropriated hundreds of millions of marks in state aid cleared by the European Union for use in eastern Germany.
A report in the Weser-Kurier newspaper said on Saturday that a large German industrial group and a utility group were considering taking over Bremer Vulkan.

"It's not easy, but it is possible," Noelle told the Welt am Sonntag. The price paid for the shipbuilder would have to be sufficient to ensure that the group's creditors would also receive something from the transaction.
Bremer Vulkan's administrator said that there was a possibility the plan could work.
"It's daring, but it's possible," Wellensiek said.
The shipyards were one of the region's largest employers and their collapse sent the unemployment rate in the area, already above the national average, sharply higher.
